subject: Combining onboarding credits + mentor stipend for Mosaik Labs

From: Susan Park <susan@venturehub.vc>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: combining onboarding credits + mentor stipend for Mosaik Labs

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Mosaik Labs loved the latency and the dev experience. We're about to accept them into our Winter cohort (starts Dec 1) and have two budget items that came up during onboarding: the program offers a $10k mentor stipend (to be used for advisor time / credits) and a separate $15k Redwood onboarding credit voucher. The founders asked whether those can be combined/stacked so the stipend can be applied as extra Redwood quota for the first 3 months of the pilot.

Two quick questions: 1) Is Redwood able to make a promotional exception to allow stacking both? 2) If not, is there an alternate path (convert stipend to a one-time dedicated discount or invoice credit) that you could offer so Mosaik gets the same runway?

We need to confirm by Nov 12 to finalize the cohort SOW. Happy to jump on a short call if easier.

Best,
Susan Park
Program Director, VentureHub
susan@venturehub.vc

--
Attachment: Mosaik_Program_Summary.pdf (application summary, 2 pages)

Team — forwarding VentureHub's ask below. TL;DR: cohort wants to stack a $15k onboarding voucher with a $10k mentor stipend and use both as Redwood quota. They need a yes/no by 11/12 for SOW. I attached the program summary and a quick usage estimate the founders sent.

Options I see (please weigh pros/cons):
- Option A: Allow stacking as-is (promo credits + stipend applied to account). Easier for the customer but impacts promo policy and could set precedent.
- Option B: Convert the mentor stipend into a short-term dedicated discount (e.g., 30% off committed capacity for 3 months) — preserves promo accounting but requires commit/invoicing changes.
- Option C: One-time invoice credit post-usage (finance-friendly) — cleaner accounting but less attractive to founders at sign-up.

Attachments: Mosaik_Program_Summary.pdf, usage_estimate.csv

Can you chime in with constraints and a recommended path? If legal or finance needs to weigh in, flag and I'll brief them.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Startups & Accelerators
Redwood Inference

Connor — thanks for flagging. My quick take: do not change promo policy to allow stacking across program vouchers and Redwood marketing credits as a general rule. That said, we should be pragmatic for strategic cohorts. Recommend we convert the $10k mentor stipend to a short-term committed discount for the pilot period tied to a minimal revenue commit to avoid revenue leakage. Example proposal: 30% off committed Dedicated capacity for 3 months up to $10k gross value; onboarding voucher remains intact as promo credits.

Key asks for that path:
- Finance confirms tax and revenue recognition (Laura)
- Legal to sign off on an addendum (no change to standard voucher T&Cs)
- Sales to confirm startup is willing to sign a 3-month committed SKU (Connor)

If finance/legal block this, fallback is a one-time invoice credit post first invoice (clean but less attractive). I'm happy to approve for cohort accounts where VentureHub is a strategic partner.

-Ben

Thanks for pulling this in. A few accounting constraints to keep in mind:

1) Promo vouchers that are issued by Redwood and applied as "prepaid credits" against hosted usage are governed by our deferred revenue rules. Stacking another promotional item that acts as a credit against usage complicates revenue deferral unless we reclassify one of the items as a discount on an invoiced SKU.

2) Converting the $10k mentor stipend into a committed-discount is workable, but only if the startup signs for a measurable committed SKU (even a small one, e.g., $3k/mo over 3 months) and we record the stipend as a contra-revenue discount. That preserves revenue recognition and avoids creating non-standard liabilities.

3) One-time invoice credits (post-invoice) are the simplest operationally — they don't touch deferred revenue mechanics — but the founders seldom like delayed credits at sign-up.

Attached is a short matrix with pricing examples and accounting treatment: PricingMatrix.xlsx (stub). Key point: if you want the founders to see the runway immediately, we should do the committed-discount path and reflect as a discount on the invoice rather than a separate promo stacking. I'll need estimated committed SKU ($/month) and expected months to run journals.

Laura
VP, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: PricingMatrix.xlsx (pricing scenarios, 1 tab)

Susan / Mosaik founders — thanks for the patience while we scoped this internally. Short answer: we can deliver the economic runway you want without changing promo policy. Proposed path (recommended):

1) Keep the $15k onboarding voucher as-is (applies as Redwood promo credits to the hosted account).
2) Convert the $10k mentor stipend into a 3-month committed discount: Mosaik signs a 3-month Dedicated pilot SKU at $3,500/month (month-to-month billed), and we apply a 30% discount on those invoices up to a $10k cap. That gives the founders immediate runway at sign-up while preserving Redwood accounting.

Next steps I propose:
- Connor to send a one-page addendum and updated SOW to VentureHub and Mosaik for signature (attached: Mosaik_SOW_draft_v2.pdf).
- Laura to confirm the contra-revenue accounting journal entry and final discount wording for the addendum.
- Ben to confirm internal approval (he's OK with cohort-level exceptions).

If that works for you, confirm and I'll route the SOW to DocuSign (link will be posted). If the founders would still prefer a simple invoice credit, call it out and we'll consider as fallback.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15m call if you want to walk through.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Startups & Accelerators
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Mosaik_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (SOW draft, includes SKU and discount table)
